query: why is maine 2nd district going to ranked choice
title: Why did Maine's 2nd District go to ranked choice? LePage won
answer: Because neither Republican Paul LePage nor Democrat Matt Dunlap won more than 50% of the votes, and Maine law then requires a ranked-choice tabulation. The count ran Nov. 9-12, 2026, in Augusta. After blank ballots and write-ins were removed, LePage finished with 50.8% to Dunlap's 49.2%, and The Associated Press called the race for him.
body:
Initial results reported to the Secretary of State showed LePage with 170,263 votes (49.9%) and Dunlap with 164,845 (48.3%), a gap of 5,418 votes out of just over 341,000 ballots. More than 6,000 ballots were blank in the race, and 123 votes went to write-in candidate Gregory Ward. LePage, a former Republican governor of Maine, declared victory on Wednesday, Nov. 4. Dunlap conceded on Thursday, Nov. 5, saying, "This isn't the result we were hoping for." The tabulation still went ahead, because state law requires it once no candidate has a majority.

The count began Monday, Nov. 9, at the Maine Department of Public Safety headquarters in Augusta, open to the public and streamed online, and was completed on Thursday, Nov. 12. With the blank ballots and Ward's votes set aside, LePage had 50.81% and Dunlap 49.18%, a margin of just over 5,000 votes. The AP declared LePage the winner that day.

Maine has used ranked-choice voting since 2018 for state and federal primaries and for federal general elections. This was the fourth time in nine years the 2nd District needed a ranked-choice runoff; retiring Democratic Rep. Jared Golden won the three earlier ones. In the U.S. Senate race, Democrat Troy Jackson won a majority of first choices over Susan Collins, so no ranked-choice count was needed there.
in_the_news: Republican Paul LePage won Maine's 2nd Congressional District after a ranked-choice tabulation finished on Nov. 12, 2026, taking the seat held by retiring Democrat Jared Golden.
